content:
inc-bot: INCIDENT P0 — Smart-routing fallback loop + retry amplification detected. 5xx spike across US regions, paging on-call @Sylvie. 
Sylvie: acked, I’m on it. spinning up incident channel and assigning roles. Maria you have metric access?
Maria: I’m looking now — Grafana shows a sudden doubling of traffic to fallback variant 'redwood/gptx-2-quant-v1' at 02:03 UTC, and us-west is failing over to eu-west repeatedly. Client retry counters show many clients retrying with short backoffs (~200-500ms).
Maria: sample log lines: 
```
req_id=7b3f1f retry=1 route=smart-routing->fallback variant=redwood/gptx-2-quant-v1 region=us-west status=502
req_id=7b3f1f retry=2 route=smart-routing->fallback variant=redwood/gptx-2-quant-v1 region=eu-west status=200
req_id=8c9d2a retry=1 route=smart-routing->fallback variant=redwood/gptx-2-quant-v1 region=eu-west status=502
req_id=8c9d2a retry=2 route=smart-routing->fallback variant=redwood/gptx-2-quant-v1 region=eu-west status=502
```
Maria: notice retry count increments and sometimes second try goes to another region — looks like server failover + client retry doubling traffic.
Kamal: probable cause: a recent routing-policy change (deploy last night) reordered fallback variants and left allow_client_retry=true. smart-routing was configured to failover to any compatible variant/region without incrementing backoff on the client side. When a variant rejects (502), smart-routing retries to another region which looks like a server-side retry while client also issues a retry -> amplification.
Sylvie: can you fetch the active policy? paste the policy blob.
Maria: active policy snippet: 
```
{"policy_name":"smart-fallback-v3","rules":[{"matcher":"latency>150ms","action":"failover"}],"fallback_variants":["redwood/gptx-2-quant-v1","redwood/gptx-2-quant-v1","redwood/gptx-2-compat-v0"],"allow_client_retry":"true","route_timeout_ms":1200}
```
Maria: note duplicate variant entry and allow_client_retry stringified true. That plus aggressive route_timeout makes server attempt failover quickly.
AJ: tagging @ProductSupport — are customers reporting errors?
ProductSupport: several high-value customers reported elevated 5xx and doubled token usage. ETA on mitigation?
Kamal: mitigation plan: 1) temporarily disable smart-routing failover globally to stop server-side failovers; 2) enable per-customer throttles/circuit-breakers on retrying clients; 3) fix policy ordering and remove duplicate variant entry; 4) increase route_timeout and flip allow_client_retry=false until we patch.
Maria: executing step 1 now — toggling smart-routing to 'prefer-local' mode via control plane. Command: 
```
curl -X POST -H "Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN" https://control.redwood/api/v1/routing/policy/_toggle -d '{"policy":"smart-fallback-v3","mode":"prefer-local"}'
```
ops-bot: Command accepted. policy_update_id=policy_4882 status=applied code=200
ops-bot: NOTE: change will propagate to runtime pools in ~15-30s.
Maria: propagation logs: 
```
2026-03-15T02:07:45Z policy_4882 apply -> queues notified
2026-03-15T02:07:52Z pool-us-west acknowledged policy_4882
2026-03-15T02:07:56Z pool-eu-west acknowledged policy_4882
```
Kamal: good — while that lands, I’ll bump circuit-breaker thresholds and enable a temporary token-based per-client rate limiter for the top 1000 API tokens.
Kamal: running kube rollout pause for smart-router to prevent in-flight changes: `kubectl annotate deployment smart-router paused=true -n inference`
Nate: pushed emergency rules to the rate-limiter: `limit: 10rps per-token burst 20 window 1m` for top tokens.
ProductSupport: posting interim status to status.redwood.io — customers will see a note about degraded performance + retries. Draft: "We are investigating increased 5xx errors and intermittent latency. Mitigation in progress."
Sylvie: handoff ETA — I need to get sleep in 40m. AJ you take next on-call window. Leave runbook: monitor 5xx, request volume to fallback variant, token-cost delta, and confirm policy fix deployed to git.
AJ: taking handoff. next_steps: 1) confirm policy file change committed (remove duplicates, set allow_client_retry=false), 2) schedule rollback window for 4h if issues, 3) notify top customers of mitigation.
Maria: committed policy fix: 
```
# git diff
- "fallback_variants": ["redwood/gptx-2-quant-v1","redwood/gptx-2-quant-v1","redwood/gptx-2-compat-v0"]
+ "fallback_variants": ["redwood/gptx-2-quant-v1","redwood/gptx-2-compat-v0"]
- "allow_client_retry": "true"
+ "allow_client_retry": "false"
```
Maria: deploying policy update to control plane now. curl returned 200. ops-bot confirmed propagation.
ops-bot: post-change healthcheck: us-west 200/200 sanity pings, eu-west 198/200, latencies trending down.
Maria: metrics: 02:03 -> 02:10 saw 72% drop in cross-region failovers and 58% drop in 5xx error rate. client retries measured by header x-client-retries dropped significantly after rate-limiter applied.
Kamal: added a temporary mitigation note to the runtime: for 30m we’ll reject immediate client retries with 429 if more than 2 attempts in <2s.
Sylvie: marking impact: partial outage for ~18 minutes for some customers, increased token consumption observed (rough estimate +35% cost for affected windows). Customer-facing severity: degraded performance, some 5xx.
AJ: documented post-incident actions: 1) add CI policy validation to catch duplicate variants and malformed allow_client_retry values; 2) add a guard that disallows server-side failover if client retry window is aggressive; 3) update SDK docs to recommend exponential backoff >=500ms and jitter; 4) run tabletop on fallback-amplification scenario.
ProductSupport: logged 6 affected enterprise customers, offered credits and a follow-up call.
Nate: closing notes: we left smart-routing in prefer-local mode and will revert to smart-fallback-v3 after we have a validated policy and client backoff guidance.
Sylvie: thanks team — handing incident to AJ for next monitoring window. I’ll be reachable if needed.
AJ: acked takeover at 03:20 UTC. monitoring until 04:00 UTC then gradual return to normal ops if stable.
inc-bot: INCIDENT UPDATE — mitigations applied, impact reduced. Incident state: mitigated -> monitoring. primary cause: routing-policy misconfig + client retry amplification. postmortem owner: AJ.
Maria: filing PR for policy schema validation and a pre-deploy CI check.
Sylvie: closing on-call note: great rapid coordination, tighten CI checks.
(Reaction :thumbsup: from AJ and ProductSupport)
